sources.citation: Richard Hammack, Wilfried Imrich, Sandi Klavžar, Handbook of Product Graphs, 2nd ed., CRC Press, 2011; Chapter 6, Cartesian Product / Factoring the Cartesian Product.
sources.verified: Publisher chapter abstract explicitly identifies the Sabidussi–Vizing unique prime factorization theorem for connected Cartesian products; book preview identifies the Cartesian-product automorphism-group section and states automorphism groups are described from prime factors.
sources.load_bearing: Unique Cartesian prime factorization and the factorwise/isomorphic-factor-permutation boundary for product automorphisms.

sources.citation: Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension and density on Johnson and Hamming graphs, Discrete Applied Mathematics 312 (2022), 29–44.
sources.verified: ScienceDirect abstract inspected; it states that the full automorphism group of H(d,q) is S_q wr S_d.
sources.load_bearing: Exact classical model: Aut(H(2,3)) = S3 wr S2, order 72.

sources.citation: John D. Dixon and Brian Mortimer, Permutation Groups, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 163, Springer, 1996.
sources.verified: Springer bibliographic record inspected; Chapter 8 is The Structure of the Symmetric Groups. The standard classification statement used here is that an imprimitive maximal subgroup stabilizing a partition into m equal k-blocks is S_k wr S_m.
sources.load_bearing: Partition stabilizers/wreath products in S_n and maximality of the imprimitive equal-block stabilizer.

sources.citation: Francesco Fumagalli and Martino Garonzi, On the primary coverings of finite solvable and symmetric groups, Journal of Group Theory 24(6) (2021), 1189–1211.
sources.verified: Peer-reviewed article text/metadata inspected. It states that imprimitive maximal subgroups of S_n are stabilizers of equal-sized partitions W_d ≅ S_d wr S_{n/d}.
sources.load_bearing: Independent modern exact statement that the 3+3 partition stabilizer in S6 is the maximal imprimitive subgroup S3 wr S2.

sources.citation: Mark V. Lawson, Inverse Semigroups: The Theory of Partial Symmetries, World Scientific, 1998.
sources.verified: Bibliographic metadata and Lawson's primer inspected. The primer states that inverse semigroup theory is based on structure-preserving partial bijections and that all partial bijections of X form the symmetric inverse monoid I(X).
sources.load_bearing: Partial/inverse-semigroup formalisms represent supplied partial symmetries; partiality is typed by domains and does not itself select a new mixed-support arrow.

sources.citation: Ruy Exel, Partial Dynamical Systems, Fell Bundles and Applications, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 224, AMS, 2017.
sources.verified: AMS book page inspected. An accessible article following Exel Definition 11.4 was crosschecked: a partial action explicitly contains domains A_g and isomorphisms alpha_g:A_{g^{-1}}->A_g, with composition on the compatible domain.
sources.load_bearing: Exact domain-and-map semantics for partial actions; a missing mixed domain/map is additional data, not generated by the word 'partial'.

sources.citation: Wilfried Imrich, Tomaž Pisanski, Janez Žerovnik, Recognizing Cartesian graph bundles, Discrete Mathematics 167–168 (1997), 393–403.
sources.verified: ScienceDirect abstract inspected: graph bundles generalize covering graphs and graph products.
sources.load_bearing: Adjacent standard framework for twisted/fiberwise transport beyond a direct Cartesian product.
